problem: Node-based topological RL navigation (HD Planner etc.) discards fine-grained geometry, end-to-end RL lacks explicit context, and pre-trained natural-image ViTs or generic SSL (DINO) transfer poorly to occupancy maps and are not navigation-aware.
motivation: Navigation in unknown environments under partial observability needs multi-scale understanding: global layout, local geometric continuity, and robustness to occlusion. A dense, navigation-specific pre-trained representation fused with graph reasoning should give better waypoint decisions at low compute for on-robot deployment.
key_idea: Pre-train a lightweight ViT context encoder on occupancy maps with three complementary self-supervised tasks (Stochastic Path Masking, FOV prediction, MAE), then fuse it with a local topological graph via hierarchical cross-attention in a SAC-trained waypoint policy.
insight: Navigation-specific pre-training is essential: generic ImageNet/DeiT ViTs underperform even having no encoder, while the multi-task encoder (13.1M params) beats DINOv2-small by 9.5 SR / 11.7 SPL on hard maps. The task ablation shows complementarity: FOV+MAE improves over either alone, FOV+SPM degrades (tension between global and local), and all three give the best result (83.9 SR / 64.7 SPL on hard).
method: Context encoder: transformer (d=512, L=6, 4 heads, patch 8) over patchified occupancy map with learnable positional encodings, trained from scratch
Stochastic Path Masking: random-walk masked patch trajectories (random ratio and smoothness) reconstructed by a lightweight decoder for global layout
FOV prediction: keep a circular core region visible and reconstruct the surrounding expansion ring for local geometric continuity
MAE: 75% random masking, encoder sees only visible patches, decoder reconstructs; each step samples one of the three tasks with equal probability
Graph state: K=20 collision-free candidate waypoints within 3 m, kNN (k=10) graph, node features = goal direction, frontier utility, visited flag

Policy: node MHSA, LSTM history query, two-stage cross-attention (context tokens then node tokens), pointer attention over nodes; SAC training with goal/step/geodesic-distance-shaping reward, encoder fine-tuned jointly

setting.backbone: Custom transformer context encoder (13.1M, SSL pre-trained) + attention/LSTM policy trained with SAC
setting.training_data: Occupancy maps from HM3D, MP3D, Gibson, HouseExpo plus programmatically generated synthetic maps for SSL; RL in the HD Planner simulator
setting.observation: 2D occupancy context map built from LiDAR SLAM plus local topological graph and goal direction
setting.action_space: Selection of one of K=20 candidate waypoint nodes, executed with DWB local planner
setting.simulator: HD Planner 2D simulation environment (maps from HM3D/MP3D/Gibson/HouseExpo) plus real world
setting.privileged: none (geodesic distance used only in training reward)

numbers.bench: other:Real-world goal navigation (Go2, 6 start-goal settings x2)
numbers.extra: Unitree Go2, Livox Mid-360, FAST-LIO2, Jetson Orin; 12 trials; success within 0.2 m, 128 step limit

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 episodes per difficulty level in unseen test environments
numbers.evidence: Table context_encoder_comparison: Ours Hard SR 83.9 SPL 64.7

numbers_note: Real-world table has no explicit split; sim splits are unnamed unseen test environments, labelled 'test'.
results: In real-world tests MacroNav reaches 91.7% SR and 73.4% SPL versus HD Planner 83.3/18.6, FAR Planner 75.0/63.7 and NavRL 16.7/14.5, with the lowest CPU/GPU usage and 0.036 s planning. In simulation the encoder beats ViT-DINO on hard maps (83.9/64.7 vs 74.4/53.0) and helps TD3 and PPO too.
limitations: Oscillatory waypoint selection in long-range navigation due to no trajectory-level optimization
Purely geometric single-frame occupancy representation without temporal or semantic cues
Small real-world evaluation (12 trials) and possible bias for layouts outside pretraining coverage / sim-to-real gap
